prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Monday October 5, 2026. Topic: Quantum, space, nuclear, robotics.

Window: Friday October 2, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Monday October 5, 2026 12:20 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. This spans 2 non-trading day(s): news published on those days (e.g. Saturday and Sunday) is in scope and often the most important. Anything published after 12:20 ET on Monday October 5, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Quantum computing (IonQ, Rigetti, D-Wave, Quantum Computing Inc, Infleqtion, IBM, Google), space (SpaceX, Rocket Lab, AST SpaceMobile), nuclear/SMR, eVTOL, robotics/humanoids, drones: technical milestones with figures, contracts, offerings, analyst actions, conferences, and each stock's move including sympathy moves.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **QBTS** — Quantum Computing
- D-Wave Quantum opened a beta program for a gate-model quantum simulator on October 1, providing early access to BBVA, FirstQFM, Florida Atlantic University, and the Jülich Supercomputing Centre; the simulator supports up to 21 qubits in ideal and hardware-emulation modes and is programmable through Ocean SDK, Quantum Circuit Description Language, and Qiskit. [report] (Ground News, Oct. 4; Startup Fortune, Oct. 4)
- D-Wave’s simulator uses dual-rail superconducting technology and is intended to support error-aware quantum programming; the company said its first dual-rail gate-model machine is planned for later in 2026. [report] (Quantum Zeitgeist, Oct. 5)

## Quantum Computing
- IBM and Harvard demonstrated learning SYK Hamiltonians with polynomial scaling, while Quantinuum reported that adiabatic evolution outperformed the fast Fourier transform for larger materials simulations. (Quantum Zeitgeist, Oct. 5)
- New Mexico’s Roadrunner Quantum Lab opened in Albuquerque with 12 initial company and national-laboratory tenants, including IonQ, Diraq, and Sandia; the facility has 35,000 square feet and $450 million in state backing. (Quantum Zeitgeist, Oct. 5)
- QUDORA Technologies began a €122 million project involving seven German research institutions and industry partners to develop a 1,000-qubit fault-tolerant quantum computer. (Quantum Zeitgeist, Oct. 5)

## **IONQ** — Quantum Computing
- Bank of America initiated coverage of IonQ with a **Buy** rating and a **$60** price target; the report was cited during the October 2–5 window, although the underlying initiation was reported earlier. (Business Insider, Oct. 4)

## **RGTI** — Quantum Computing
- Rigetti closed at **$15.25** on Friday, October 2. (Live Trading News, Oct. 5)

## **QBTS** — Quantum Computing
- D-Wave closed at **$15.77** on Friday, October 2. (Live Trading News, Oct. 5)

## **ASTS** — Wireless & Mobile
- AST SpaceMobile shares closed at **$58.45** on Friday, October 2, up **2%** for the session; the stock was reported approximately **1% higher overnight** late Sunday into Monday after T-Mobile removed “with Starlink” from its consumer satellite-service branding. [rumor] (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 5, 01:44 ET)
- The reported T-Mobile branding change involved removal of “with Starlink” from the T-Satellite logo and introductory website language; the item was attributed to PCMag and was not presented as a change to AST SpaceMobile’s carrier agreements. [report] (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 5, 01:44 ET)
- AST SpaceMobile’s existing agreements with AT&T and Verizon were reported as preserved under a formalized joint venture involving AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon; the venture is intended to pool spectrum resources and expand satellite coverage. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 5, 01:44 ET)

## **RKLB** — Space
- Rocket Lab signed a 20-mission Electron launch agreement with Japanese Earth-observation company Synspective covering **2028–2031**; the agreement was described as Rocket Lab’s largest commercial Electron contract and increased Synspective’s total bookings to **47 missions**. [report] (Ground News, Oct. 5)
- The Synspective agreement was reported to increase Rocket Lab’s contracted backlog above **$2.3 billion** and Electron backlog above **100 launches**. [report] (Startup Fortune, Oct. 2)
- NASA’s Mars Telecommunications Network contract award to Blue Origin was reported as paused, with Rocket Lab’s formal protest to the Government Accountability Office still unresolved. [report] (Advanced Television, Oct. 5, 10:00 ET)
- Rocket Lab’s Neutron maiden-flight timing was reported as uncertain, with the 2026 launch window narrowing and a potential slip into 2027; the company had not officially announced a delay. [report] (Advanced Television, Oct. 5, 10:00 ET)

## Space
- SpaceX reportedly completed three launches and four booster landings in under 13 hours, carrying four astronauts, 130 commercial payloads, and a classified intelligence satellite. [report] (Ground News, Oct. 5, 07:06 ET)
- SpaceX’s reported Friday share price was **$158.96**, up **7.35%** for the session; SpaceX is not a publicly listed U.S. equity ticker in the cited report. [report] (Ground News, Oct. 5, 07:06 ET)
- The reported SpaceX launch activity included NASA’s Crew-13 mission, a Google satellite deployment, and a classified National Reconnaissance Office payload. [report] (Ground News, Oct. 5, 07:06 ET)

## Quantum Computing
- Friday, October 2 closing prices cited for the broader quantum group were **$15.25** for Rigetti and **$15.77** for D-Wave; the available results did not provide a complete, consistently sourced October 2–5 price set for IonQ, Quantum Computing Inc., IBM, or Google. (Live Trading News, Oct. 5)
